When Should You Buy DoorDash Stock?

Shares of DoorDash (DASH) have lost 33.8% over the past twelve months, a period when the S&P 500 returned 15.3%. The stock now sits 36.7% below its highest close of the past year, even though the company posted sales growth in each of its last four reported quarters. Has the fall made DoorDash cheap, or is buying now still too early?

DoorDash Now Costs About Half As Much On Sales

A lower share price and a year of 33.6% sales growth have combined to make DoorDash cheaper on a sales basis than it has usually been. At the end of September, the shares traded at 5.0 times twelve-month sales. That multiple is about half the 9.7 times recorded a year earlier, and the stock had traded lower at only 9 of the 24 quarter ends since 2020.

Underlying business operations did not weaken over the twelve months ending in June. During that period, DoorDash reported an operating margin of 4.8%, slightly above the 4.6% recorded a year earlier. The June quarter itself stands as the exception, producing a 3.5% operating margin compared to 5.0% a year earlier.

The stock looks significantly more expensive on profit than on cash. At the October 26 close, DoorDash traded at 87.0 times earnings against 25.9 times operating cash flow. In other words, the company's operations bring in far more cash than it reports as profit.

How Much Growth Are DoorDash Buyers Paying For?

Forecasts for the next report indicate growth will remain near the 35.6% pace DoorDash reported for the June quarter, rather than accelerating. Analysts expect revenue of $4.66 billion for the third quarter of 2026, about 35% more than a year earlier. The company describes this growth as broad. In its release for the June quarter, DoorDash said its marketplaces, membership programs, and monthly active users all grew strongly in the first half of 2026 against a year earlier.

What Could Buying DoorDash Before November Cost You?

Buying before November means accepting a reaction to results that has historically moved in both directions. DoorDash will report its third-quarter 2026 results in November 2026. Over the two trading days following each of its last six reports, the stock rose three times and fell three times. The largest move was a 14.2% fall after the November 2025 report, while the most recent was a 4.3% gain after the August 2026 report.

A wider sell-off represents the other cost of buying early. During the 2025 tariff shock, DoorDash fell 23.0% from peak to low, compared to 19.0% for the S&P 500. Additionally, news reports on October 26 said DoorDash was in advanced talks to acquire Instacart. Those reports said a deal could be completed as soon as this week, before the November report. Neither company has confirmed the talks, and the test below covers only the November results, not the deal.

title: Target makes a big mistake with its latest pricing decision
detail:
Target makes a big mistake with its latest pricing decision
Maurie Backman
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 8:33 AM MST 4 min read
TGT
WMT
COST
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Target used to be known as a place to get fun, unique products at reasonable prices.

But shoppers went to Target more so for the selection than the savings.

Target has long trailed behind competitors like Walmart and Costco on price, and for a long time, that wasn't an issue. That's because Target's inventive products were so much of a draw that customers were willing to bust their budgets a bit to load up a full cart.

These days, shoppers are being more cautious with their money. With inflation up 3.7% on an annual basis, according to the most recent Consumer Price Index, the old joke about walking into Target for milk and leaving with a $100 shopping cart isn't as funny.

But it's not just an affordability issue. Target has fallen out of favor with customers due to issues like disorganized stores, empty shelves, and employees who don't seem happy to be there. 

Now, Target is taking steps to make its products more affordable. But that's not necessarily the right approach toward winning customers back.

Target moves forward with price cuts

Target recently announced that it's lowering prices on nearly 2,000 home, apparel, and accessories products ahead of the holiday shopping season. 

The move builds on more than 10,000 price reductions Target says it has made over the past year.

"Guests are looking for great products at an incredible value, and that's an important part of what we aim to deliver every day," said Cara Sylvester, executive vice president and chief merchandising officer, Target. 

"By continuing to lower prices across our assortment, we're making it even easier for busy families to create moments of joy this fall with the style, design and exceptional value they can only find at Target."

The discounts could of course help price-conscious families, particularly as they prepare for the holidays. But Target's challenges extend beyond the price tags on its shelves.

Target has also expanded its merchandise offerings.Target
Target needs more than cheaper merchandise

Target needs to rebuild its reputation for differentiated merchandise, improve inventory availability, and give customers compelling reasons to choose its stores over competitors.

The good news is that the company has spent months trying to sharpen its identity around style, design, and value. And during the company's most recent earnings call, CEO Michael Fiddelke said Target was encouraged by customer responses to its merchandising changes.

But Sylvester was candid about two important categories.

"If I turn to home and apparel, just to be clear, we are not satisfied with the performance in either of those businesses, and there's more work ahead in 2027 and beyond," she said during the earnings call.

title: DoorDash nears $17 billion deal to acquire Instacart, report says

DoorDash nears $17 billion deal to acquire Instacart, report says
Proactive

DASH

WMT
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

DoorDash Inc (NYSE:DASH) is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart (NASDAQ:CART) in a deal that could value the business at about $17 billion, as the US food delivery group seeks to expand its presence in the grocery market.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter, that an agreement could be finalized as soon as this week, although there is no guarantee the negotiations will result in a transaction.

The potential acquisition would combine DoorDash's extensive restaurant and retail delivery network with Instacart (NASDAQ:CART)'s established relationships with grocery retailers, strengthening its position against competitors, including Walmart and Amazon.

DoorDash has expanded beyond restaurant orders into groceries and other retail products, and said it had more than 200,000 grocery and retail stores on its marketplace.

Instacart operates a marketplace covering more than 2,200 grocery brands and 100,000 stores, giving DoorDash access to a substantial network of retail partners.

The potential deal comes as delivery platforms seek growth beyond restaurant orders and face pressure from rising labour costs, tighter regulation of delivery workers and competition from retailers building their own online services.

Instacart generated $3.75 billion in revenue last year, compared with DoorDash's $13.72 billion.

The companies have not announced a completed transaction, and the reported negotiations remain uncertain.

Shares of DoorDash (DASH) fell 6.1% on Monday, October 26, 2026, during a session in which the S&P 500 gained 0.7%. The drop occurred on the day news reports said DoorDash was in advanced talks to buy its delivery rival Instacart. How big is the deal DoorDash is reported to be discussing?

What Would DoorDash Pay For Instacart?

News reports on October 26 said a potential agreement would value Instacart at roughly $17 billion, compared with DoorDash's market value of $73.2 billion at that day's close. People familiar with the matter said a deal could be announced as soon as the week of October 26. Neither company has confirmed the talks, and any deal would likely face antitrust review.

Reports that Instacart was exploring a sale first ran on Friday, October 23, and Instacart's stock surged that day. A news report on October 24 said Uber and DoorDash were circling, and that one of the two had already walked away. Instacart competes with major retailers in the grocery delivery market, and the reported talks took place as DoorDash expands beyond its restaurant delivery roots. Analysts quoted in one report said a possible deal is about keeping up with Walmart and Amazon.

Did DoorDash Fall With Other Consumer Stocks?

No. The consumer discretionary sector fund, XLY, rose 1.0% during the same session, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8%. Target fell 2.8%, the largest drop among DoorDash's five peers, while Amazon.com rose 0.4%. DoorDash fell more than twice as far as any of its peers: the stock moved on its own rather than with its broader group.

Where DoorDash Stock Stands After The Drop

A decline of this size is not rare for DoorDash. The stock experienced six falls at least this large in the prior 365 days, with the latest being a 7.7% drop on September 28, 2026. Monday's drop also immediately followed a 3.5% fall on Friday, October 23.

Over the 12 months to October 26, DoorDash stock lost 33.8%, while the S&P 500 returned 15.3%. The shares closed that day at $168.44, well below the 52-week closing high of $266.06 set on October 29, 2025, but still above the closing low of $146.60 from March 27, 2026. Over the past month alone, from September 25 to October 26, the stock lost 12.9% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.8%.

DoorDash is valued at 4.6 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared with 3.2 times for the S&P 500. The company is expected to report its fiscal Q3 2026 results in November 2026. Revenue growth, 35.6% from a year earlier in fiscal Q2 2026, is the measure to watch in that report.

title: If You Invested $1000 in Walmart a Decade Ago, This is How Much It'd Be Worth Now
detail:
If You Invested $1000 in Walmart a Decade Ago, This is How Much It'd Be Worth Now
Zacks Equity Research
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 4:30 AM MST 3 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

How much a stock's price changes over time is a significant driver for most investors. Not only can price performance impact your portfolio, but it can help you compare investment results across sectors and industries as well.

The fear of missing out, or FOMO, also plays a factor in investing, especially with particular tech giants, as well as popular consumer-facing stocks.

What if you'd invested in Walmart (WMT) ten years ago? It may not have been easy to hold on to WMT for all that time, but if you did, how much would your investment be worth today?

Walmart's Business In-Depth

With that in mind, let's take a look at Walmart's main business drivers.

Walmart Inc. has evolved from a traditional brick-and-mortar retailer into a global omnichannel retailer. Its stores, clubs, e-commerce sites, mobile applications, delivery services and membership programs allow customers to shop across physical and digital channels. The company also uses marketplace, advertising, fulfillment and data capabilities to extend its retail ecosystem.

The Bentonville-based company operates supercenters, discount stores, Neighborhood Markets, Sam's Clubs and e-commerce platforms. Its merchandise spans grocery, consumables, health and wellness, general merchandise, apparel, home products and electronics. Walmart also sells merchandise under private-label brands such as Equate, George, Great Value, Holiday Time and Mainstays, along with licensed brands.

Walmart operates in the United States, Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India and Mexico. The company has more than 10,900 stores across 19 countries and serves approximately 280 million customers and members each week through stores and eCommerce websites. Walmart generated revenue of $713 billion in fiscal 2026 and employs approximately 2.1 million associates worldwide.

The company reports three operating segments: Walmart U.S., Walmart International and Sam's Club U.S. Walmart U.S. includes retail and eCommerce operations in the United States and Puerto Rico. Walmart International consists of retail, wholesale and eCommerce operations outside the United States. Sam's Club U.S. operates membership warehouse clubs in the United States and Puerto Rico and includes samsclub.com.

In fiscal 2026, Walmart U.S. accounted for 68.1% of revenues, Walmart International represented 18.5%, and Sam's Club represented 13.4%. Walmart continues to expand digital capabilities across these businesses through store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, marketplace services, advertising, membership programs and automated fulfillment. These capabilities are increasingly integrated with the company's physical network and support a seamless omnichannel customer experience and broader digital engagement over time.
